subject.title: fix(browser): prove post-action target continuity before adopting a tab

question: Must this PR preserve extension-relay renderer-swap continuity through a relay-owned stable public handle before merge, or should that owner-specific contract be designed and landed separately before replacing the current recovery path?
rationale: The branch correctly rejects unsafe route inference, but choosing whether stale raw IDs are an acceptable relay behavior versus requiring stable relay handles defines the public browser target contract and cannot be safely decided by an automated repair.

options.title: Complete relay-owned continuity
options.body: Require relay-stable target handles, focused relay route coverage, and real shared-tab proof before merging this behavior change.

options.title: Pause for a narrower owner design
options.body: Do not merge the branch until browser owners specify and separately land the extension-relay identity contract that callers can rely on through detach and reattach.

recommendation.title: Complete relay-owned continuity
recommendation.body: Require relay-stable target handles, focused relay route coverage, and real shared-tab proof before merging this behavior change.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical report specifies the intended cross-backend target-identity contract and requests browser-owner confirmation for this exact relay/MCP boundary.
